summary: Couch Investor argues that while all attention is on Nvidia after Huang's departure, several names he owns could benefit. He rejects the Intel comparison, arguing Nvidia is still innovating while Intel a decade ago did little but pay executives, buy back overvalued shares and pay a dividend; he believes Nvidia's teams and roadmap are strong, though the five-to-ten-year outlook is less certain, and he questions a board with no semiconductor or AI background. He notes the anti-Nvidia trade — AMD rising from the low $400s to $550 and Broadcom up — and neocloud weakness, with Nebius down 13% on the day; he owns Nebius and CoreWeave and is waiting until after Nvidia's 17 November earnings, arguing interim CEO Colette Kress's reported opposition to Jensen's OpenAI and neocloud investments should not hurt prepayments. His four picks are Alphabet (GOOGL) BUY near $300, at 21.1 times forward earnings, with Google Cloud and TPUs growing and capex growth slowing towards a free-cash-flow inflection; Meta (META) BUY at 21.5 times trailing and 19.1 times forward earnings, with earnings expected to grow about 28%, 21.7%, then 19.2%; Micron (MU) BUY, flipped from CONDITIONAL_BUY after he added in the low $700s, at 4.3 times forward earnings, with HBM demand making a near-term peak unlikely and a return towards $1,000 possible; and Broadcom (AVGO) BUY, flipped from CONDITIONAL_BUY. Nvidia itself is UNCERTAIN: he waits until after the 17 November earnings, though it trades at just 13.2 times forward earnings with fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast at 90.8%.
title: Nvidia Is Falling. These 4 Stocks I Own Could Win From It
